#606. Sutton's predictions v Waffle the Wonder Dog and his owner Simon

Manchester City have won their first seven Premier League games of the season but will their 100% record survive Saturday's trip to an improving Aston Villa side?

"Villa have beaten City in this fixture in each of the past three years under Unai Emery," said BBC Sport football expert Chris Sutton.

"They will fancy it this time too - they are seven unbeaten in all competitions, and flying at the moment."

Sutton is making predictions for all 380 Premier League games this season, against AI, BBC Sport readers and a variety of guests.

For week eight, he takes on Waffle the Wonder Dog and his owner Simon, who is played by actor James Merry.

Waffle's After School Club, featuring James and Waffle, is available on CBeebies and BBC iPlayer right now, with lots of fun after-school adventures for families to enjoy together.

Do you agree with their predictions? You can pick your own below.

The most popular scoreline selected for each game is used in the scoreboards and tables at the bottom of this page.

A correct result (picking a win, draw or defeat) is worth 10 points. The exact score earns 40 points.

Want to make more predictions? You can play BBC Sport's new Match of the Day predictor game every week, featuring six fixtures from domestic and European competition.

Waffle's After School Club often ends in mayhem and mess despite the best efforts of Simon. How will the pair get on at predictions?

Waffle is a talking dog whose adventures on his show often end in chaos for Simon and the rest of his family.

Like most dogs, he loves football - or at least loves chasing one.

"I am an enthusiastic baller," Waffle told BBC Sport. "But technically my best position is right-back... on the sofa.

"My favourite player is the England captain, Harry Kane-9, and I'm a Liverpool fan so my all-time hero is Kenny Dog-leash.

"My fur is red and I am a poodle so of course I support the Reds, or Liverpoodle as I like to call them - they never walkies alone."

Waffle loves watching Liverpool on Match of the Day. "It's past my bedtime on a Saturday night, so instead I like to watch them on iPlayer after an early Sunday morning garden wee."

In real life, actor James Merry is an Aston Villa fan, who has a long connection with the club.

"I grew up in Sutton Coldfield, north Birmingham, and just about everyone is Villa there," he told BBC Sport.

"My mum's side of the family are all fans - my great-aunt was a season-ticket holder for about 40 years and my nan lived most of her life on Witton Road, which is just round the corner from Villa Park.

"My first job was there too - when I was 16 I worked in the catering department serving burgers on matchdays.

"Then, during the summer I had to clean every executive box and polish all the cutlery and make sure everywhere was properly stocked.

"We had the run of Villa Park and I was like a kid in a candy shop."

Chris Sutton, Waffle the Wonder Dog and James Merry were speaking to BBC Sport's Chris Bevan.

The AI predictions were generated using Microsoft Copilot Chat - we simply asked the tool to 'predict this weekend's Premier League scores'.

So, I am up against a talking dog this week? I'm not sure that improves my chances of winning - I've been barking up the wrong tree with my predictions all season anyway.

One of us has got to beat AI though - I've been reading about it in the news and it is not just with football scores where it seems to be taking over.

This game is a tough one to call, though. It is going to be very tight.

Nottingham Forest can't score. That's their issue, and they have only managed five goals in their first seven league games.

It did make me laugh when I read that Forest boss Oliver Glasner had got Chris Wood to give advice to the other strikers about finishing - why not just play Wood then?

Ipswich are still bottom of the league table based on my predictions (see bottom of page) but they ran Manchester City close in the end last week and are doing better than everyone expected, myself included.

I like what Tractor Boys boss Gary O'Neil is doing there, and they already have three league wins from seven games - the last time they were in the Premier League, in 2024-25, they only managed four all season.

Forest are second bottom and could really do with getting something here, and Ipswich haven't drawn a game yet - so that's what I am going for.

James' prediction: The director of Waffle, Tim Hopewell, is a Forest fan and I have gone for them here. I like the way they play. 1-2

Villa have hit a bit of form and seem to be getting back to the level they were at last season.

They had another good win in the Champions League this week, but then you'd expect them to beat Viking pretty comfortably.

Emery's side played well against Newcastle last week too but I thought Newcastle were a bit too gung-ho, and paid the price. City are a lot more streetwise.

City are going to slip up eventually this season but the fact they have lost on their past three visits to Villa Park actually makes me think it will be different this time.

Erling Haaland is fit too, which will obviously help. With all the heat on the club at the moment it could just turn out to be one of those seasons where they continue on this incredible run.

Waffle the Wonder Dog's prediction: Ross BARKley gets two for Villa, but Erling HOWLand to score a hat-trick. Sorry, dad! 2-3

James' favourite Villa players: The early to mid-'90s was the time when I was getting into football so Dean Saunders and Dalian Atkinson were my heroes, and Paul McGrath as well. That was certainly a golden era - I need to mention Shaun Teale too, because he was always a favourite. I think I had his name on the back of a shirt.

Now? I think most people of my generation would pick John McGinn. He is an absolute club legend for what he has done for us down the years and my shirt now has got McGinn on the back.

James on Villa's season: We seem to be picking up some form after another slow start. It looks like Johan Manzambi is going to be pivotal for us this season and Nicolas Jackson has started well, he has stuck a few away.

This might sound a bit bonkers but, with Emery's record in Europe, I am more excited about that than what we might do domestically, because I think we might go deep in the Champions League.

James' prediction: Because we are weak at the back at the moment I think City will score two or three, but we are looking lively up front and could do the same. I've got to be partisan - and I am also going to go for a barnstormer. 3-2

Arsenal were so ugly in the way they beat Nottingham Forest last weekend, but were a lot easier on the eye in the midweek draw with Bayern Munich.

They are going to be without the injured Bukayo Saka for this game, but they are at home and they should still have too much for Everton.

Everton will make it tough for them, of course, but I am not sure how they will hurt the Gunners.

James' prediction: Arsenal are just a machine at home. 3-1

Whoever loses this is likely to end the day in the relegation zone.

Sometimes these kind of games can be quite cagey, with both teams afraid of being beaten, but here I feel like Coventry and Fulham will have a go and there could be a few goals flying in.

Coventry have a bit about them going forward, especially when they use their pace on the counter-attack, but they are also a bit vulnerable defensively.

Because of that, I am going to go with Fulham. They got their first win of the season against Hull last week and they are definitely capable of getting another one here.

James' prediction: My old man is a Coventry fan - he was born and bred in Cov but then married a Brummie and moved to Birmingham so he was always on a hiding to nothing trying to get me to support Coventry. He won't be happy because I've gone for a draw here. 1-1

We were talking on the Monday Night Club about what Chelsea could do this season without any European football.

Tottenham are not in Europe either, of course, but they don't look like they are going to be challenging at the top of the table the way Xabi Alonso's side are.

People keep saying how Chelsea's attack is so good, but their 2-0 win over Everton last time out was their first clean sheet of their campaign in the league, and that side of thing still needs to improve.

Spurs, meanwhile, do seem to be getting better, albeit slowly.

It was a big result for them to beat Coventry on Monday but they have an awful record at Stamford Bridge, with only one win there in the Premier League era.

I don't see them getting anything this time, either.

Waffle the Wonder Dog's prediction: Archie GrayHOUND will score a couple for Spurs, but I'm backing Chelsea because I was a fan of Didier DOGba back in the day. 4-2

James' prediction: Chelsea carry so much attacking threat. 3-1

Crystal Palace manager Pierre Sage's future appears to be in some doubt but his critics seem to have forgotten that they are 14th in the table, when the Eagles finished 15th last season under Oliver Glasner.

Yes, Palace had a heavy defeat at Brighton last week and it doesn't help it was at the hands of their big rivals, but it is not like Sage has got one point from his first seven games. They are leaking a few goals, but there are reasons for that.

There has been huge change at Selhurst Park in recent months, with some key players leaving, especially at the back. Others have stayed but are still unhappy, and Sage has had a lot to contend with.

Palace play in Turkey on Thursday night which won't help their preparation for this game, but I still feel like they will get something against Newcastle.

There has been a lot of change at the Magpies too, but the thing that worries me most about Matthias Jaissle's side is that they are so open.

'Chaotic' was the word I used to describe them against Aston Villa last week.

Villa are always very well structured in the way they play but they got chances against Newcastle just by persevering with their build-up play.

If Newcastle don't get their press quite right again here, then Palace will cause them problems too - I definitely don't see this game as being one where defences are on top.

James' prediction: Both teams will be happy just to get a point on the board. 1-1

Although Hull have made a great start I still think they will get relegated.

We know they will have a go at Brentford, but the Bees will be too smart for them.

Brentford would have beaten Liverpool last week without Yehor Yarmoliuk's stupid red card. If they can keep 11 men on the pitch, they will win this one.

James' prediction: Brentford are such an amazingly well-run club with what they have achieved. They are going to be too strong for Hull. 1-2

Liverpool have an extra 48 hours to prepare for this game - they played Villarreal at home on Tuesday, while Brighton are away in the Czech Republic on Thursday.

I don't think it will make any difference, though, because the way that the Seagulls play, I am expecting them to go to Anfield and win.

This has the makings of a great game but, while Liverpool have had a couple of good results, I am still not convinced by them.

Andoni Iraola's side are a work in progress with a tendency to empty their midfield and that means Brighton can hurt them.

Waffle the Wonder Dog's prediction: A win for the Liverpoodles! 2-1

James' prediction: This is going to be close. Brighton are playing really well but I am still going to back Liverpool at Anfield. 2-1

After all the stick I got from Manchester United fans for saying they would get thumped by Leeds last weekend, it turns out I was only a few days out - it happened against Como instead.

United have been poor all season, though. That's why I went for them to be despatched like that - the 5-0 scoreline was a little bit tongue in cheek, but the point I was making has been proven this week.

The Bruno Fernandes criticism of Michael Carrick just adds to the problems United have at the moment - it is as if they are at the stage now where you have to pick who you want to back.

I don't know where United go from here but I am going for a Bournemouth win - the Cherries will attack them, and their great recent record at Old Trafford will give them confidence too.

If United do lose, I think it will be the end for Carrick because I just don't see how he survives this.

Even if United get something from this game, it is still just a matter of time before he goes.

Waffle the Wonder Dog's prediction: BARKus Rashford to win this for United. 2-1

James' prediction: Carrick really needs a win and they are at home so I think he will get it. 2-0

Sunderland have killed me this season because I just don't seem to be able to predict them at all.

The Black Cats are bottom of the table after losing four league games in a row and their boss Regis le Bris has a few problems to solve.

One of them is having European football that stretches their squad - they are away in Poland on Thursday - but at least they will have striker Brian Brobbey back from injury at the weekend.

After last weekend's loss at Bournemouth, Sunderland defender Nordi Mukiele suggested the Black Cats may have become "arrogant", but I don't see that outburst being as damaging as the ones by Manchester United players recently.

Still, things like that are better kept inside the dressing room because some of Mukiele's team-mates will be asking him if he was calling them arrogant.

I was never arrogant as a player, by the way, but people used to call me far worse than that in my day.

Maybe we will see a reaction from Sunderland here, but I still don't see them winning this because Leeds are battle-hardened and are a good team too.

They weren't at their best against Manchester United but still picked up a point, and they won't be leaving the Stadium of Light empty-handed.

Waffle the Wonder Dog's prediction: I like the sound of LEADS United and I love playing with George the cat (who lives next door) but 11 Black Cats means it's hide-behind-the-sofa time! 0-2

James' prediction: I had a look at all the fixtures and I thought one of them has got to finish 0-0, hasn't it? I have gone for this one. 0-0

Chris and the BBC readers both got six correct results with no exact scores from the 10 games in week seven, giving them 60 points apiece.

His guest, boxer and Ipswich fan Fabio Wardley, did better with four correct results, including one exact score - Bournemouth's 2-0 win over Sunderland - for a total of 70 points.

But, for the third week in a row, AI took the weekly win.

It managed eight correct results, including one exact score - Liverpool's 2-1 victory at Brentford - for a total of 110 points.

Like last week, there was only one game where everyone picked the right outcome - Brighton's 5-0 victory over Crystal Palace - although again hardly anyone got the correct score.

From almost 30,000 predictions, the most popular scoreline was a 2-0 Seagulls win. Almost 8,000 of you went for that, but well done to the 57 of you who got it spot-on.

#607. On this day in space! Oct. 21, 2008: India launches its 1st mission to the moon with Chandrayaan-1

Get full access to premium articles, exclusive features and a growing list of member rewards.

India swung for the moon with Chandrayaan-1, its first deep space mission.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

On Oct. 21, 2008, the Indian Space Research Organization launched its first mission to the moon. The mission was named Chandrayaan-1, and it consisted of both an orbiter and an impactor.

Chandrayaan-1 launched from the Satish Dhawan Space Center on an Indian rocket called the Polar Satellite Launch Vehicle, or PSLV-XL. (Launch occurred at 8:52 p.m. EDT, though it was about 6:22 a.m. local time at the launch site on Oct. 22.)

It arrived in lunar orbit about three weeks later and dropped off the Moon Impact Probe, which crashed into the moon on Nov. 14. The rest of the Chandrayaan-1 spacecraft stayed in orbit, where it collected and transmitted data from the moon to Earth for about a year. The mission ended abruptly 14 months ahead of its planned end date when scientists lost contact with the probe.

The Indian Space Research Organisation, or ISRO, had a lot riding on the success of Chandrayaan-1 moon mission, which marked the first-ever deep space mission by the Indian space agency. It was also the first mission to the moon for India, a country that hopes to launch its own crewed spacecraft and build a space station.

Chandrayaan-1 did more than just demonstrate that India's space program was capable of launching missions to the moon; it also returned some amazing science results, like evidence of water ice on the moon.

"In September 2009, scientists published results of data collected by the American M3 instrument which had detected absorption features on the polar regions of the surface of the Moon usually linked to hydroxyl- and/ or water-bearing molecules," NASA said in a mission overview.

The spacecraft carried 11 instruments to study the moon, five of them built by ISRO. The rest were experiments for the European Space Agnecy and NASA.

"In addition to the five Indian instruments, the spacecraft carried scientific equipment from the United States, the United Kingdom, Germany, Sweden, and Bulgaria," NASA said.

It took until Nov. 8, 2008 for Chandrayaan-1 to enter lunar orbit, where it stayed until contact was lost in August 2009, most likely due to a power supply failure caused by overheating.

"This was short of the spacecraft’s planned two-year lifetime, although ISRO noted that at least 95% of its mission objectives had been accomplished by then," NASA wrote.

India did not stop at the moon with Chandrayaan-1. In 2019, the country launched the Chandrayaan-2 orbiter, which carried the Vikram lander and Pragyan rover. Chandrayaan-2 reached lunar orbit successfully, but the Vikram landing failed.

The Chandrayaan-3 misson followed in 2023, which successfully landed a new Vikram lander and Pragyan rover near the moon's south pole. India plans to launch the Chandryaan-4 mission to return moon samples to Earth in 2028.

Want more space history? Check out our full On This Day In Space Story archive and watch our On This Day In Space videos on YouTube.

Hanneke Weitering is a multimedia journalist in the Pacific Northwest reporting on the future of aviation at FutureFlight.aero and Aviation International News and was previously the Editor for Spaceflight and Astronomy news here at Space.com. As an editor with over 10 years of experience in science journalism she has previously written for Scholastic Classroom Magazines, MedPage Today and The Joint Institute for Computational Sciences at Oak Ridge National Laboratory. After studying physics at the University of Tennessee in her hometown of Knoxville, she earned her graduate degree in Science, Health and Environmental Reporting (SHERP) from New York University. Hanneke joined the Space.com team in 2016 as a staff writer and producer, covering topics including spaceflight and astronomy. She currently lives in Seattle, home of the Space Needle, with her cat and two snakes. In her spare time, Hanneke enjoys exploring the Rocky Mountains, basking in nature and looking for dark skies to gaze at the cosmos.

#608. Knicks Owners Address Backlash to Championship Ring Phishing Email

The New York Knicks' owner confirmed that Madison Square Garden corporate employees received a phishing test using the 2025-2026 Championship ring as bait, admitting the mass email was "unfortunate."

The Knicks organization is on defense after a corporate airball.

Months after the New York team's NBA title win against the San Antonio Spurs June 13, the team's owner MSG Sports confirmed employees who support the team at Madison Square Garden received a phishing test that falsely offered staff a fitting for a championship ring.

"The company had previously sent out an email to its corporate team as a simulation of a phishing attack designed to strengthen our security against hackers," an MSG Sports spokesman told E! News Oct. 23. "MSG was recently hacked and extorted using an employee login and password obtained through a similar phishing attack."

Still, the company—which also operates the Garden—acknowledged that implementing the security exercise was a misstep.

As the statement said, "Using the rings as a lure to gain employees attention was an unfortunate mistake."

But as the Knicks aim to bounce back with their corporate teammates, they're also on the rebound from a foul with assistant coaching staff. According to The Athletic, key leadership who helped players like Jalen Brunson and Karl-Anthony Towns clinch game five were given empty boxes with no commemorative jewelry inside at an Oct. 20 ceremony.

In turn, the organization has publicly released its nearly $4 million plan for distributing the rest of the rings, while all of the athletes from the 2025-2026 team were gifted their bling during the celebration.

"The company is gifting more than 275 championship rings and jewelry to players, coaches, employees and other members of the Knicks family," the press release from MSG continued, "worth more than $3.7 million."

The statement noted that the priceless trinket was "in recognition of their contributions and celebrating this achievement."

Despite the major league drama, relive the Knicks' slam-dunk season with all of their celebrity superfans.

When it comes to Timothée Chalamet's fandoms, his love of the New York Knicks reigns supreme."My grandma was a huge Knicks fan, so that's what turned me onto them," the Marty Supreme star told 7PM in Brooklyn in 2025. "If you live in New York, you are a Knicks fan."

And if you've been keeping up, then you know Kylie Jenner has been joining Chalamet, whom she's dated since 2023, courtside to cheer on the Knicks.

You could never sever Ben Stiller's tie to the Knicks. In fact, the Severance director said that if he could choose between winning an Oscar or having the team take the championship title, he'd pick the latter."I really think, at the end of the day, if I knew that I had the choice, I would give it to the Knicks," he said on New Heights in 2025, "because I knew at least I had the choice in this weird, non-real situation."

Spike Lee is a longtime Knicks superfan and believes the 2025-2026 roster has what it takes to secure the trophy."I don’t care about San Antonio. OKC,” the filmmaker told the New York Post in May 2026. “We’re going to win.”

Nothing could rock Tracy Morgan's love for the Knicks. As the 30 Rock alum put it on The Rich Eisen Show in 2021, "I'm the biggest Knicks fan there is besides Spike."

Live from New York...it's Pete Davidson. The Saturday Night Live alum has often been seen sitting courtside.

Chris Rock's loyalty to the Knicks is no laughing matter as the comedian has attended many games over the years.

Larry David isn't going to curb his enthusiasm for the Knicks.

And neither is his costar JB Smoove."How it started vs How it ended," the actor wrote on Instagram in 2024. "It’ll always be Knicks for life."

Jordyn Woods' love for the Knicks extends on and off the court. The Woods by Jordyn founder is engaged to the team's center Karl-Anthony Towns.

While Cardi B has a song called "Bodak Yellow," she's all about that orange and blue. In fact, the rapper and former Patriots player Stefon Diggs officially debuted their romance at a 2025 game between the Knicks and the Boston Celtics.

Is Anne Hathaway wearing the  Chanel boots Knicks colors? Yeah, she is. The Devil Wears Prada star showed where her loyalties lie by donning an orange and blue pocket square to The Tonight Show in April 2026.

"I’m very chill," she told host Jimmy Fallon about her fandom. "I’m very loving and calm. But I’m also the type of fan that I considered wearing an OG jersey out here today."

Speaking of which, Fallon is also a big fan of the Knicks, with him even bringing his eldest daughter Franny along for the ride during the 2026 NBA playoffs.

You don't have to travel back to the future to see how much Michael J. Fox loves the Knicks. The actor has gone to many games with his wife Tracy Pollan.

Throughout the Knicks' ups and downs, Jon Stewart has continued to support the team, with The Daily Show host calling himself a "ride or die" fan.

A Knicks win is music to Maggie Rogers' ears as the singer has documented her love for the organization.

#609. 31 best horror movies on Prime Video thatll give you nightmares

In the mood for something scary? There's nothing quite like the fresh thrill of a great horror movie. That tingle that runs down your spine. The goosebumps that prick at your skin. The hard, cold thumping that hits your heart. Yet seriously scary is only one flavor of horror, a genre that welcomes pestering poltergeists and wicked witches alongside lovable zombies and creepy kids. Whatever kind of mood you're in, we've got a pick for you, right from Prime Video.

The library of Prime Video is vast but ever-changing, so we've scoured their stacks to curate a current collection sure to thrill, chill, and delight. Whether you want soul-scorching psychological thrillers, haunted house horror, spine-tingling classics, modern masterpieces, or something as ghoulish as it is goofy, we've got you.

Here are the best horror movies now on Prime Video.

This 2018 Suspiria remake has been described by director Luca Guadagnino and star Tilda Swinton as a "cover" of Dario Argento's 1977 classic — exploring rather than mimicking Argento's perspective on supernatural horror. With this mission in mind, Suspiria is a gratifying watch that exemplifies how identical genre tropes can be employed for disparate emotional effects. Yes, it's all fear, but fear of different kinds that present an unsettling experience unto itself. — Alison Foreman, Entertainment Reporter

How to watch: Suspiria (2018) is now streaming on Prime Video.

Six years after George A. Romero modernized the horror genre by injecting political allegory into it with Night of the Living Dead, Deathdream tackled the ongoing nightmare of the Vietnam War by telling the story of a soldier killed in action who nevertheless goes and returns to his family home, albeit a changed man. Very changed. Specifically, he is now one who sits around in sunglasses all day and then goes out and steals people's blood via syringe every night.

Director Bob Clark (best known for the holiday duology of A Christmas Story and Black Christmas) and his Children Shouldn’t Play With Dead Things writer Alan Ormsby were the masterminds behind this deeply disturbed folk tale, which turned the very real PTSD that returning veterans and their families were going through into the stuff of symbolic and scary horror. — Jason Adams, Entertainment Reporter

How to watch: Deathdream is now available to rent or purchase on Prime Video.

Although Matt Reeves’ 2010 American remake Let Me In is better than it has any right being, the 2008 Swedish original from Tinker Tailor Soldier Spy director Tomas Alfredson cannot be beaten — yes, even if you take into account the hilariously bad CG cat attack scene.

One of the greatest vampire movies ever made, Let the Right One In is basically just that infamous line from Notting Hill ever so lightly twisted, where it’s a “girl” standing in front of a boy asking him to love her... which can be a grim business when the girl is a literal bloodsucker. Ain’t love grand? — J.A.

How to watch: Let the Right One In is now available to rent or purchase on Prime Video.

Admittedly, the Terrifier movies aren’t for everybody. As they appeal to the most depraved and hardcore of horror movie fans, we don’t recommend this to anyone whose idea of the ultimate spooky night in front of the TV is watching Alfred Hitchcock’s Rebecca. Not a knock against Rebecca, which is grand. It's just that these movies are scratching very, very different itches. The scratches that the Terrifier movies deliver will leave a whole lot of oozing skin flaps on the floor.

I can’t even say that these movies, which detail the sadistic impulses of the unhinged Art the Clown as he bounces from one victim to the next, are “good” per se. But the second one is far more accomplished (and far less sexist) than the first, and the bit that’s come to be known as “the bedroom scene” giddily reigns in gore-hound hell for a reason. — J.A.

How to watch: Terrifier 2 is now available to rent or purchase on Prime Video.

Almost 15 years on, it still shocks me that Evil Dead sicko maestro Sam Raimi managed to make a horror movie as utterly disgusting and deranged as he did with Drag Me to Hell while scoring a PG-13 rating. I think the people at the MPA must’ve had a curse-happy Mrs. Ganush (Lorna Raver) on their own tails that they were trying to appease!

And yet as much fun as this movie is, and as widely platformed as it was, it was still a box office flop — our culture has so much to learn. For those of us who’re in the know, though, this is one of Raimi’s creepiest crawliest efforts. Once it straps you down, the ride it takes you and poor helpless bank officer Christine (Alison Lohman) on as she attempts to get a curse off her back is relentless, right up until its shocking final frames. — J.A.

How to watch: Drag Me to Hell is now available to rent or purchase on Prime Video.

Want more film and TV news and reviews delivered straight to your inbox? Sign up for Mashable’s Top Stories newsletter or get Mashable push alerts today.

You’d think that having somebody as preternaturally gorgeous as Cillian Murphy sit down next to you on an airplane would be a blessing! But Wes Craven said heck naw to that with Red Eye, his 2005 airplane thriller. Craven might be best known for slasher franchises like Nightmare on Elm Street and Scream. On its surface, Red Eye might seem a different path, but it is still very much playing with the tropes that Craven had mastered in the subgenre he helped shape (twice).

As Lisa (Rachel McAdams) realizes that the great big blue eyes of her seatmate – the hilariously named Jackson Rippner (Murphy) — are actually creepy and not sultry as originally advertised, Craven ratchets up the tension and the claustrophobia quick. And McAdams turns in yet another super underrated performance as a regular woman driven to extremes by Rippner’s bizarre and violent demands. The kind of movie the poster blurb “A real rollercoaster ride!” was invented for. — J.A.

How to watch: Red Eye is now available to rent or purchase on Prime Video.

Before you die, you should see The Ring! That’s how that tagline goes, right? Well close enough, and we won’t even enforce any seven-day time limit on you. Take that, impatient-girl-down-the-well. Gore Verbinski’s smash 2002 remake of Hideo Nakata’s 1998 J-horror classic kicked off a whole wave of creepy long-haired girls stalking about here in the States, but per usual it was all downhill from the start.

One of the best horror films out of the Aughts, The Ring stars Naomi Watts as a journalist and a mom whose investigation into a creepy cursed videotape leaves a trail of mangled-face corpses in its wake. Watts loves herself a horror remake (see also Funny Games and Goodnight Mommy) but, again, The Ring remains the high-water mark. And Verbinski loads this sucker up with instantly iconic imagery. Just try to stand in front of a circular mirror brushing your long, black hair and not immediately picture centipedes, I double dog dare ya. — J.A.

How to watch: The Ring is now available to rent or purchase on Prime Video.

An extremely underrated entry in the found footage genre, 2014’s As Above, So Below (from Quarantine director John Erick Dowdle) drags us kicking and screaming deep down into the creepy catacombs rotting beneath modern-day Paris. As filmmakers have exclaimed for ages, “Location! Location! Location!” And it doesn’t get better than that.

Taking the baton from Neil Marshall’s masterpiece The Descent, this movie has its characters spelunking down crumbling nightmare corridors, ones that have our hair standing on end even before the monsters start showing up. As for the monsters? The last act when all is revealed has proven divisive, but I personally dig it. (Pun most certainly intended.) — J.A.

How to watch: As Above, So Below is now available to rent or purchase on Prime Video.

There’s a whole world of cinema out there to explore, and thankfully each and every person on the face of the planet is also afraid of zombies. This Paris-set undead apocalypse thriller from director Dominique Rocher finds actor Anders Danielsen Lie working in a somewhat different register than The Worst Person in the World or his other work with director Joachim Trier. Here he plays Sam, who wakes up after a raging house party trapped inside a fancy 6th arrondissement apartment building, besieged on all sides by brain-hungry ghouls.

Running out of food and sanity in equal measure, Sam makes friends with the downstairs neighbor (Denis Lavant) who is a great listener, mostly because he’s a zombie trapped behind a metal gate. The Night Eats the World is more character-focused than our American zombie flicks tend to be, and all the more despairing because of it. — J.A.

How to watch: The Night Eats the World is now streaming on Prime Video.

Senegalese writer/director Nikyatu Jusu made a massive first impression with her feature debut Nanny, a psychological horror film reminiscent of Repulsion but steeped in the unease of the immigrant experience. Anna Diop stars as Aisha, an undocumented immigrant living in New York City who takes on the child-rearing duties of Rose (Rose Decker), the daughter of a well-to-do Manhattan couple (played by Michelle Monaghan and Morgan Spector).

Aisha is desperate to make enough money to bring her own son to the U.S. from Senegal, where she had to leave him behind. But tormented by disturbing visions of drowning, Aisha starts coming undone, and when Rose’s mother becomes an enemy, things grow increasingly unsettling for everybody. — J.A.

How to watch: Nanny is now streaming on Prime Video.

We do love ourselves a "seaside town with a secret" horror story (see also: Messiah of Evil), and 1981’s Dead & Buried ranks up there among the creepiest of them all.

Based on the novel by Chelsea Quinn Yarbro and adapted by Dan O'Bannon and Ronald Shusett (who co-wrote Alien), Dead & Buried is perched somewhere between The Fog and Re-Animator. Dead & Buried tells the tale of Potter's Bluff, a small town on the California coast where the locals can't seem to stop themselves from brutally murdering all of the tourists. ("Living the dream," coos any NYC resident.) Awash in that musty barnacled atmosphere that lovers of this subgenre live for, this classic's got the bloody goods. — J.A.

How to watch: Dead & Buried is now available to rent or purchase on Prime Video.

If Vogue released an issue in collaboration with the Necronomicon, its contents might resemble something like director Nicolas Winding Refn's The Neon Demon. Starring Elle Fanning as a doomed ingénue, this stylish fever dream explores the Los Angeles modeling scene for an indictment of Western beauty standards and commercialization that's as captivating as it is biting. — A.F.

How to watch: The Neon Demon is now streaming on Prime Video.

The first three of the four total [REC] films are streaming on Amazon, and we thoroughly REC-comend that you watch all of them. They're very different movies but all a blast in their individual ways. That said, there's no place better to begin than the beginning, and there's no scarier place to be than right inside Jaume Balagueró and Paco Plaza's terrifying found-footage masterpiece that kicks off the series.

Following ace on-the-scene TV news reporter (and final girl icon) Ángela Vidal (Manuela Velasco) on a routine assignment covering a firehouse, we watch a boring story become anything but as Ángela and her cameraman Pablo (Pablo Rosso) find themselves trapped inside an apartment building with a horde of bloodthirsty rampaging undead. Notable for one of the greatest all-time ending scares, one that has been ripped off mercilessly ever since. — J.A.

How to watch: [REC] is now available for rent or purchase on Prime Video, as is [REC] 2.

Often, when horror movies are set on college campuses, they're schlocky slashers with sorority sisters being ripped to shreds. Here, however, writer/director Mariama Diallo spins a unique horror story about the ghosts of America's past and how they still haunt us. At a prestigious university, lore lingers of a lynched witch who still causes chaos. Freshman Jasmine Moore (Zoe Renee) believes she is the latest victim, but Professor Gail Bishop (Regina Hall), who has just been appointed the first Black master of the university, begins to suspect the insidious evil isn't supernatural. Is it just racism? Her quest to understand the seedy underbelly of the school leads her to uncomfortable places and harrowing realizations. With a shadowy atmosphere and a creeping sense of dread, Diallo submerges us into the mindset of her haunted heroes. — Kristy Puchko, Film Editor

How to watch: Master is now streaming on Prime Video.

Don’t miss out on our latest stories: Add Mashable as a trusted news source in Google.

Writer-director Jordan Peele done gone and done it again with this "Watch the skies!" horror, which somehow smashes up Hollywood history with evil alien shenanigans, whilst also sneaking in a message about racialized invisibility beside the blood rain and face-eating chimpanzees. And if you’re keeping count, that makes the man fully three-for-three after Get Out and Us, putting him by my estimation already among the ranks of horror masters such as John Carpenter and David Cronenberg. We will look back on this run with astonishment in a couple of decades.

Keke Palmer and Daniel Kaluuya star as animal trainer siblings mourning their father as a strange presence simultaneously makes itself known in the clouds above his ranch. Nope escalates into absolute madness as it rockets toward its surreal WTF of a conclusion. And with every Peele joint comes a new iconography, be it “the Sunken Place” or red jumpsuits and golden scissors. After Nope, I doubt any of us will ever be able to look at those little strands of colored flags or those dancing air tube men ever the same. Not to mention chimpanzees wearing party hats. — J.A.

How to watch: Nope is now available for rent or purchase on Prime Video.

From the phenomenally twisted mind of Clive Barker, the original Hellraiser is as scary today as it ever was. Descend into this puzzling world of monstrous torture (see what I did there?) with genre icon Pinhead, played by Doug Bradley, facing off against protagonist Kirsty, played by Ashley Laurence. No matter where you stand on the most recent Hellraiser installments, it's hard to deny that this 1987 nightmare is an all-time great. — A.F.

How to watch: Hellraiser is now streaming on Prime Video.

You can’t really call Event Horizon “Hellraiser in space” because the Hellraiser franchise did actually go into outer space with its fourth film titled Bloodline (which you should not under any circumstances watch). But Event Horizon is kinda sorta “Hellraiser in space” anyway. Hell, it’s a far better “Hellraiser in space” than Hellraiser: Bloodline ended up being!

Telling the very Alien-sounding tale of a crew of space-jockeys (led by Laurence Fishburne, Kathleen Quinlan, Joely Richardson, and Sam Neill) who stumble upon a distress signal that would’ve been best left un-stumbled-upon, Paul W.S. Anderson’s film is shockingly gruesome for a big-budget picture with so many name actors aboard. Nobody expected to see the nice scientist from Jurassic Park claw his own eyes out! And yet that’s just the tip of what Event Horizon has in store for you. — J.A.

How to watch: Event Horizon is now available to purchase on Prime Video or stream via add-ons.

The middle film in Italian maestro Dario Argento’s “Three Mothers” trilogy — sandwiched between 1977’s master-work Suspiria and 2007’s decidedly-not-a-masterwork Mother of Tears — Inferno usually receives a mixed reception, but I’m here to say “No!” (That’s “no” in Italian.) Is Inferno absolute nonsense from start to finish? Of course it is. I couldn’t even begin to summarize the story, which skips back and forth between Rome and New York City and involves so many red herrings that you could repopulate the oceans and still have leftovers for Friday Night Fish Fry. I’ve seen this movie half a dozen times, and I still have no idea what happens in it.

But it’s some of the most stylish and spooky nonsense you’ll ever see, pushing Suspiria’s already bursting technicolor palette past its breaking point, then around the globe and past it a second time for good measure. — J.A.

How to watch: Inferno is now available to rent or purchase on Prime Video.

If religious horror is what your dark heart desires, then your prayers are answered with Saint Maud. Critics heralded writer/director Rose Glass's feature film debut as a horror masterpiece, and it's easy to see why. Morfydd Clark gives a riveting and nerve-rattling performance as Maud, a hospice nurse who's tasked with caring for the body. But her bigger goal is to save the soul of her decadent new patient. Amanda (Jennifer Ehle) doesn't believe in God, but does believe in a good time. Her sensuality concerns and enchants Maud, pulling the two into a bond that will turn bitter and brutal. Weaving real religious rituals into the seductive spin of psychological horror, Glass creates a descent into hell that is a twisted delight to watch. — K.P.

How to watch: Saint Maud is now available to rent or purchase on Prime Video.

We have no less than David Cronenberg to thank for one of the best Stephen King adaptations! Cronenberg and Christopher Walken, anyway, who made for a terrific team — shame those two never worked together again; there’s something irresistibly perfect about their weird union. But maybe that lightning could only strike the once, so celebrate the once we will.

In The Dead Zone, Walken stars as Johnny Smith, a man who gets in a car accident and gains the ability to see people’s futures by shaking their hand. And that’s called “science” — look it up. Of course this gift turns out to be nothing but a curse, and before you know it, he’s firing rifles at politicians using babies for human shields. Que sera sera, and such. — J.A.

How to watch: The Dead Zone is now available to rent or purchase on Prime Video.

What would a horror hits list be without a little Vincent Price? Though the actor reportedly disliked his work being defined as outright “horror,” this unforgettable face of fear appeared in more than 200 TV shows and films, including many of the scariest releases of the mid-20th century. Price's pointed features, slicked-back hair, and pencil mustache have been mimicked and referenced in countless horror homages.

Though Price properly assumed the throne of horror king with the surprise success of House of Wax (1953), his later starring role in House on Haunted Hill (1959) offers a more complete vision of his legacy. Plus, famed B-movie director William Castle’s flick makes early use of the haunted dinner party premise, a particularly goofy trope that would pop up for decades, from Clue (1985) and The Last Supper (1995) to You're Next (2011) and Ready or Not (2019).* — A.F.

How to watch: House on Haunted Hill is now streaming on Prime Video.

Tim Robbins stars as a Vietnam vet losing his shit and then some in this nightmarish 1990 Adrian Lyne thriller.

Sandwiched between Fatal Attraction and Indecent Proposal in Lyne’s sexy filmography, this one surely stands out, mostly because of all the tentacles. But the tentacles are made kind of sexy in Lyne’s hands, so it doesn’t actually stand out quite as much as you’d think! Especially in the infamous dance scene with Elizabeth Peña — playing a character named “Jezebel” because of course — where she gets her lusty groove on with some half-glimpsed hell monster. Still, Lyne proves deft at mixing his usual gauzy theatrics with squishy surrealism, and there are several images in Jacob’s Ladder that prove terrifyingly unforgettable. — J.A.

How to watch: Jacob’s Ladder is now available to rent or purchase on Prime Video.

The second film out of four total Body Snatchers tales (if you don’t count things like The Stepford Wives or the TV series BrainDead, which are variations on the theme) is also the best. Donald Sutherland stars as a health inspector in 1970s San Francisco (“That is a rat turd!”) who, along with his co-worker (Brooke Adams), discovers that pod people from outer space are taking over humanity (just roll with it).

Director Philip Kaufman took the conspiracy thrillers of the decade (movies like The Parallax View and Three Days of the Condor and added a good dose of sci-fi goopiness, milking the paranoia of the post-Nixon era quite literally. And extra praise must be heaped upon the supporting cast of Jeff Goldblum, Veronica Cartwright, and Leonard Nimoy — not to mention an all-time great freak-out ending. — J.A.

How to watch: Invasion of the Body Snatchers is now available to rent on Prime Video via add-ons.

Directed by Yeon Sang-ho, Train to Busan imagines the end of the world as a screamingly entertaining explosion of zombie mayhem and societal commentary brought on by a chemical spill. Terrifying, funny, and consistently original, this apocalyptic adventure is one of those films worth watching every single time you think of it. Seriously, it never gets old. — A.F.

How to watch: Train to Busan is now available to rent or purchase on Prime Video.

Why not revisit the original Voorhees-venture that kicked off all of the -ki-ki-ki -he-he-he’s in the first place?

Before Jason had his hockey mask – heck, before we knew what a Jason was —there was nice little old lady Pamela Voorhees (Betsy Palmer) in her warm woolen sweater, giving camp counselors a helpful ride … straight to hell!

The first crest in the slasher wave created by Halloween two years earlier, nobody thought Sean S. Cunningham’s little movie would be anything, including Cunningham himself. But 60 million dollars later, a legion of sequels and rip-offs and plush dolls have proven everyone very wrong. Turns out we were all waiting for Kevin Bacon to get an arrow shoved through his esophagus, we just didn’t know it yet. — J.A.

How to watch: Friday the 13th is now available to rent or purchase on Prime Video.

A secret lurks beneath the surface of this claustrophobic thriller. Written and directed by Zach Lipovsky and Adam B. Stein, Freaks begins with a surly little girl and her harried father hiding in a ramshackle house. Despite paternal warnings, Chloe (Lexy Kolker) is determined to venture outside, befriend the girl across the street, and get a frosty treat from the ice cream truck that’s always just out of reach. But she’s only beginning to understand the dangers beyond her door. Why they must hide hangs on a sci-fi twist that makes this mysterious movie distinctly satisfying and marvelously mind-blowing.* — K.P.

How to watch: Freaks is now available for rent or purchase on Prime Video.

If you relish a hidden gem of horror, you'll treasure this intimate indie ghost story. It all begins on a dark, snowy night when a teen girl (Zelda Adams) goes missing. Her single mother (Toby Poser) is deeply devoted, not only to finding her child but also to manifesting a reckoning if someone has hurt her. Her search for answers brings her close to a new neighbor (John Adams), who is haunted by a horrible secret ... and something more spirited. A lean and mean horror-thriller, The Deeper You Dig is even more fascinating when you know its three stars are wife, husband, and daughter, and that this is one of several movies they've written, directed, and starred in together as Wonder Wheel Productions. Let this be your gateway into their wild world of films. — K.P.

How to watch: The Deeper You Dig is now streaming on Prime Video.

Found-footage aficionados know that digging through a lot of dreck is part of the gig; for every gem you’ll have to watch 10 duds. And even among the gems there are a lot of crutches the sub-genre leans on that you have to submit yourself to in order to get yourself to the scares. The biggest hurdle of all being the question: “Why the hell are these people filming everything and not running away for their lives?”

Hell House LLC, which follows a group of kind of irritating youths setting up a haunted house attraction in a house that, whoopsie, turns out to be legitimately haunted, isn’t great at answering those questions. You have to meet it on its own terms. But if you’re willing to make the effort, it’s chock-full of nightmare imagery — all of those dressed-up prop dummies they find in the basement that keep popping up in new places? Fuel for a million bad dreams. — J.A.

How to watch: Hell House LLC  is now available to rent or purchase on Prime Video.

As Aliens was to Alien, so went Wolf Creek 2 to Wolf Creek — a bigger, meaner, wilder action-rollercoaster that took the smaller, subtler scares of the original and shot them off like a rocket.

Writer-director Greg McLean amps everything up to 13 in this high-octane sequel to his 2005 Aussie outback slasher masterpiece, turning serial-killer Mick Taylor (John Jarratt) into a dusty Terminator who gets into outrageous Mad-Max-esque road fights that somehow escape the notice of the authorities every time. Not as scary as the original classic, no, but a hell of a lot of nasty fun. — J.A.

How to watch: Wolf Creek 2 is now streaming on Prime Video.

What even is there left to say about George A. Romero’s horror masterpiece at this point on, 55 years after its release? That it created a new movie monster — there were "zombies" before, but not the way we know them today, which is entirely thanks to Romero. That it earned 250 times its original budget in its original release, revolutionizing independent cinema. That it’s a politically-minded molotov cocktail, sneaking in a message of racialized horror under its stark black-and-white surface.

But most of all 55 years on, this story of seven strangers stranded in a farmhouse while the world turns to ghouls outside is still, somehow against all odds, utterly terrifying. I’ve watched little Karen turn on her mother with that gardening trowel more times than I could count, and it still sends all of the shudders down my spine anyway. — J.A.

How to watch: Night of the Living Dead is now streaming on Prime Video.

What if zombie bites weren’t all bad? More specifically, what if a nip from the undead would give the impotent new life below the belt? That’s the preposterous premise that kicks off this gleefully bonkers South Korean comedy. The Park family is scraping by running a battered gas station when their fortunes are turned by a zombie (Jung Ga-ram) with a rejuvenating bite. That’s just the first act of director Lee Min-jae’s playful horror-comedy. Family hijinks, ghoulish action, gross-out gags, and absurdly earnest romance also pop up, making for a movie that is chaotically charming and pleasantly unpredictable.* — K.P.

How to watch: Zombie for Sale is now streaming on Prime Video.

*denotes that the blurb appeared in a previous Mashable list. Recommended deals for you HBO Max — top pick for premium content Disney+ — best for families Hulu — popular choice for originals Peacock — low-cost choice for live sport

#611. Scientists finally uncover why statins can cause muscle pain

Statins are among the most important medications for preventing cardiovascular disease. By lowering cholesterol, they have helped save millions of lives and reduce the likelihood of heart attacks and strokes. However, these benefits can come with unwanted effects. Some patients develop muscle pain or weakness, while a small number experience serious muscle breakdown that can potentially cause kidney failure.

Scientists at the University of British Columbia (UBC), working with colleagues at the University of Wisconsin-Madison, have identified a molecular mechanism that helps explain these complications. Their findings, published in Nature Communications, could guide the development of safer statins that maintain their cholesterol-lowering benefits while minimizing muscle damage.

How Statins Trigger a Harmful Calcium Leak

To investigate what happens inside muscle cells, the researchers used cryo-electron microscopy, an advanced imaging method that allows scientists to examine protein structures in remarkable detail. Their investigation centered on the ryanodine receptor (RyR1), a protein that regulates the movement of calcium within muscle cells.

Under normal conditions, this protein functions as a controlled gateway, releasing calcium when muscles need to contract. The researchers found that statins can interfere with this process by holding the channel open. As a result, calcium escapes continuously into areas where it should be carefully regulated, creating conditions that can injure muscle tissue.

"We were able to see, almost atom by atom, how statins latch onto this channel," said lead author Dr. Steven Molinarolo, a postdoctoral researcher in UBC's department of biochemistry and molecular biology. "That leak of calcium explains why some patients experience muscle pain or, in extreme cases, life-threatening complications."

Three Statin Molecules Reveal the Mechanism Behind Muscle Damage

The researchers concentrated on atorvastatin, a commonly prescribed medication for lowering cholesterol. Although this particular drug was the main focus, their results suggest that similar interactions could occur with other medications in the statin family.

One of the most striking discoveries was the unusual way statin molecules attach to the calcium channel. Rather than acting individually, three molecules occupy a specific pocket within the protein. The first binds while the channel is closed, making it more likely to open. Two additional molecules then enter the pocket and hold the channel open, allowing calcium to continue leaking.

"This is the first time we've had a clear picture of how statins activate this channel," said Dr. Filip Van Petegem, senior author and professor at UBC's Life Sciences Institute. "It's a big step forward because it gives us a roadmap for designing statins that don't interact with muscle tissue."

This detailed understanding could give drug developers a way to address the problem at its source. By modifying the specific features of statin molecules that interfere with muscle proteins, scientists may be able to reduce unwanted effects without compromising the drugs' ability to control cholesterol.

A Potential Path Toward Safer Cholesterol Drugs

More than 200 million people worldwide use statins. Although severe muscle injury occurs in only a small percentage of patients, less serious problems such as soreness, weakness, and fatigue are considerably more widespread. These symptoms can be disruptive enough that some people discontinue their medication, potentially losing important protection against cardiovascular disease.

The discovery could eventually help researchers create treatments that are easier to tolerate, allowing more patients to continue taking medications that reduce their risk of heart attacks and strokes.

Achieving this level of understanding required exceptionally detailed imaging. Working with the high-resolution macromolecular cryo-electron microscopy facility at UBC's faculty of medicine, the team was able to observe precisely how statin molecules interact with the muscle protein. These structural insights connect a longstanding drug safety concern to a specific molecular process, providing valuable information for future medication development.

"Statins have been a cornerstone of cardiovascular care for decades," Dr. Van Petegem said. "Our goal is to make them even safer, so patients can benefit without fear of serious side effects."

Although additional research and drug development will be needed before these findings translate into new treatments, they offer a promising direction. For millions of people who depend on statins to protect their hearts, future medications with fewer muscle-related complications could make treatment more comfortable and improve everyday quality of life.

Materials provided by University of British Columbia. Note: Content may be edited for style and length.

#613. Italy cuts air traffic in half amid data transmission issue

Citing problems with the data transmission network, Italian authorities have drastically reduced the volume of flights in their airspace. The ENAV authority ruled out malicious activity and said flights remained safe.

Air travelers across Italy faced delays and cancellations on Friday because of a problem with the country's air traffic control systems.

The ENAV air traffic control authority ruled out foul play such as a cyberattack, and said it was forced to introduce temporary restrictions of the volume of flights after identifying a data transmission problem.

Major airports in cities like Rome and Milan warned of likely disruptions and advised passengers to check with their airlines.

ENAV said it first identified the issue overnight. It was forced to restrict the volume of flights at around 6 a.m. (0400 GMT/UTC) as the number of scheduled services increased.

"We would like to inform you that this morning we guaranteed the greatest possible number of departures, including intercontinental flights," ENAV said.

Shorter-distance services were more likely to be interrupted.

"Despite the anomalies encountered on the data transmission network, we are deploying all available resources to minimize disruption and restore full operations as soon as possible," ENAV said. "We confirm an operational capacity of 50% of total air traffic, ensuring maximum safety at all times, which remains the Company's top priority."

ENAV said it had ruled out the possibility of the disturbance being caused by "malicious acts."

Rome airports operator ADR warned passengers that "flight delays and cancellations may occur" and advised passengers to contact their airline if uncertain. Milan airports company SEA issued a similar notice.

#614. A Ballon d'Or campaign as fierce off the pitch as on it

Ousmane Dembele won the Ballon d"Or in 2025 and is one of 10 PSG players listed for it this year

An emotional Ousmane Dembele had barely settled back into his chair at Paris' historic Theatre du Chatelet last September, gold-dipped orb in hand, when campaigns for this year's men's Ballon d'Or prize began to whirr into action.

Entourages roused their candidates, media revelled in the hype. Who deserved the award in 2026? A World Cup year, no less, in which the narrative occasionally became not just which players could lead their country to glory, but how doing so would help them secure football's biggest individual accolade.

"The Ballon d'Or has been discussed every single day," said European football expert Guillem Balague on BBC Sport's Euro Leagues podcast.

"Quite clearly it follows the pattern of society, where it puts a lot of emphasis on the individual - it's harder to understand why a collective works, it becomes very easy to understand why one dribbles or doesn't dribble."

Clamour for the spotlight only increased as the red-carpet ceremony neared.

"You can't underestimate the PR machine that some clubs and some players are going to use," added French football journalist Julien Laurens.

Managers and sporting directors talked up their charges, and questioned why others on their squad did not make the 30-man shortlist.

Deco branded it a "huge scandal" that Barcelona pair Raphinha and Pedri missed out, but backed Lamine Yamal as overwhelming favourite to win it. Not, he says, because he is also a Barca player, but "because I like football".

Star names have appeared frequently in the media. Lamine Yamal himself insisted he will not "beg for anything" - after last year saying he dreamed of "winning many" - but suggested the prize should not merely go to the top goalscorer.

Paris St-Germain manager Luis Enrique confessed he is "bored of the Ballon dâOr" - although with a record 10 PSG players on the shortlist, perhaps he wishes to keep out of the debate. Dembele and Khvicha Kvaratskhelia talked each other up to BBC Sport.

"We can cut it in two," joked Dembele. "Honestly, he deserves it, the season he had was exceptional." Kvaratskhelia responded: "Of course it's him!"

A 'Kvara d'Or' campaign in Georgia celebrated the country's favourite fleet-footed son.

"I think for the big nations it's really difficult to understand what [winning] would mean for the small country," the winger explained.

Kylian Mbappe, who Real Madrid boss Jose Mourinho compared to the original Ronaldo, was less subtle than most in his pitch to win the award for the first time.

"I always think I'm the best but everyone has their own opinion," professed the Frenchman, now the all-time World Cup top goalscorer. "Of course, this year could be good for me to win the Ballon d'Or - but journalists vote."

Indeed - since a short spell of national team captains and managers also voting ended in 2015 - the 30-player shortlist drawn up by the publications France Football and L'Equipe has been voted on by one journalist from each of the top 100 Fifa-ranked nations.

The deadline has passed. The winner has already been chosen.

What does it mean to win the Ballon d'Or?

James Kirkham, a sports brand strategist who has worked with top clubs and players, including Harry Kane, says the build-up has had an election feel.

"You're going out, canvassing, getting your vote and making sure you shore up certain blocks from certain countries, and why wouldn't you?" adds Kirkham.

The lobbying is not for everyone. Max Eberl, Bayern Munich's board member for sport, championed Kane and Michael Olise but said the best players, external "are the ones who don't need to run a campaign".

Mbappe's compatriot, Jean-Pierre Papin, winner of the award in 1991, meanwhile told French TV:, external "I like Kylian a lot, he's a record-breaker. However, there comes a point when it's all about me, me, me and me."

Mbappe did make an interesting observation, alluding to the dominance of Lionel Messi and Cristiano Ronaldo - the pair won a combined 13 in a 15-year period between 2008 and 2023.

"My idea of the Ballon d'Or comes from the Messi and Ronaldo era - you don't give it to ordinary players, you give it âto players who are different," explained Mbappe.

AC Milan's Kaka was the last recipient before Messi and Ronaldo's tug-of-war began, the Brazilian pipping the young pair to the prize in 2007.

That was a year after fledgling social media platforms Facebook and Twitter launched to the public. Nokia dominated mobile phone markets, people took digital cameras on nights out.

The world had changed immeasurably by the time Messi won for an eighth time in 2023.

"Today everything moves at the speed of light," explains former AC Milan chief executive and sporting director Ariedo Braida, who witnessed the club land seven awards, from Ruud Gullit to Marco van Basten's treble, George Weah, Andriy Shevchenko and Kaka.

"Fans follow individuals - the players - rather than the club themselves. It's a widespread phenomenon, which we see, for example, in politics too.

"Once upon a time, you'd be a Milan fan and go to watch Milan. Today, everything is live and with the Champions League you always get to see all the great stars straight away.

"I must say this makes me feel a bit nostalgic, because the event is always immediate. Anticipation creates that sense of longing which has now disappeared."

Are fans now more invested in star names than clubs?

Messi and Ronaldo's brilliance, and often tribal online following, has also driven an increased emphasis on individual records - among fans, media and the players who grew up dreaming of emulating them.

"You could argue we are in a more interesting time because for basically 15 years it was Messi v Ronaldo and it certainly feels more open. It is a different play now," adds Kirkham.

"The social noise is deafening, relentless, all-consuming - every fan has an insatiable appetite, every point is riffed on, reacted to, but you also have this domino effect in microcosms of the media on every platform."

Clips go viral - a great goal, magical piece of skill, a dazzling dribble - but so do opinions.

"Now a solitary word on a broadcast can get played out as tweets, reacted to by creators and ex-players in video content that exists on reels and shorts and stories, that gets back-played through radio and on TV screens," adds Kirkham.

"It's the whole ecosystem, the manner in which it amplifies across these different spaces and platforms, then it generates narratives.

"No-one is doing anything wrong, creating something they believe is resonating with their audience. But en masse that is a machine, a fierce output that is generated for a player or against a player or whatever that may be."

Braida, who was at Barcelona when Messi won the 2015 prize, would agree: "These days, media exposure is absolutely crucial. With the advent of social media, the world has changed radically compared to my day.

"There's been a global transformation, and today we live in a small global village, because with the internet you can reach everywhere in real time."

Harry Kane reflects on potential Ballon d'Or success

Michael Owen tells a story about how when Liverpool boss Gerard Houllier rang to break the news he had won the award in 2001, the 22-year-old did not even know what the Ballon d'Or was.

Owen engaged in a photoshoot at Liverpool's Melwood training ground a fortnight before the images were distributed to the media, with the striker officially presented the trophy on the Anfield pitch before a game against Derby County.

He was the first winner playing for an English club since Manchester United's George Best in 1968, the period in between dominated by Italian, Spanish and German teams.

From its launch in 1956 until 1995, when Weah became the first and so-far only African player to win it, only European players were eligible.

Only in 2007 did the award became truly global, open to players from any club - not just those representing European teams. Not until 2011 was it awarded at a glamorous ceremony. And only in 2018 was the women's prize launched.

"Winning the Ballon d'Or has an extremely positive impact," adds Braida. "We at AC Milan bought Kaka for around 7.5m euros and sold him for 67m euros [to Real Madrid].

"I must tell you, however, that in 2008, following his Ballon d'Or win in 2007, Manchester City made us a written offer of 105m euros. We're talking about a written offer, not a sounding-out or mere words.

"We were probably still in the early stages of certain commercial developments at that time, but now it clearly has a massive impact. Even back then, his value increased fivefold and winning the Ballon d'Or brought him global exposure and fame."

For someone like Three Lions captain Kane, hoping to become the first English winner in 25 years and only the fifth of all time, the prestige is huge - especially with the ceremony held in London to mark the 70th anniversary of Stanley Matthews winning the inaugural prize.

"It would be a massive achievement if it did happen," Kane said on Wednesday, having remained coy on his own chances.

Kane has done his share of recent interviews but others, such as Rio Ferdinand on Bayern's official social accounts, have made his case for him. "Ballon d'Or!"

He is, after all, vying to become Bayern's first winner since Karl-Heinz Rummenigge's second successive triumph in 1981. Not since Borussia Dortmund's Matthias Sammer 30 years ago has it returned to the Bundesliga.

Bayern will also remember the case of Robert Lewandowski, who was widely tipped as favourite in 2020, scoring at an astonishing rate as the Bavarians won all six trophies available, including the Champions League, before the ceremony was cancelled because of the Covid-19 pandemic.

The Poland striker, who finished runner-up to Messi the following season, told BBC Sport last year the prize has become "part football, partly politics" and was "more commercial" than its counterpart, The Best Fifa Men's Player award.

Ballon d'Or snubs can cut deep. Franck Ribery said it felt "like a robbery" when he missed out to Ronaldo in 2013. Real Madrid boycotted the 2024 ceremony when they learned Manchester City midfielder Rodri would scoop the gong instead of Vinicius Junior.

"In Brazil, the hype is also giant," explains Caique Andrade, international football reporter at Globo. "When Vini didn't win the 2024 Ballon d'Or, there was a lot of commotion about it."

It may be an individual award, but winning is huge for clubs, too.

"This means an incredible impact in terms of popularity, visibility and also financial returns for the club," explains Braida. "Today, with the rise of social media and followers - factors that shape commercial aspects - this is even more true."

Kirkham concludes: "It is a global point - that means more audience and more eyeballs, and that means more money around the world."

#615. A first for CRISPR: powerful prime editing alters DNA directly in the human body

Thank you for visiting nature.com. You are using a browser version with limited support for CSS. To obtain the best experience, we recommend you use a more up to date browser (or turn off compatibility mode in Internet Explorer). In the meantime, to ensure continued support, we are displaying the site without styles and JavaScript.

Heidi Ledford reports for Nature from Seattle, Washington.

The method called prime editing can make fine-scale edits to DNA (artist’s illustration).Credit: Patrick Landmann/Science Photo Library

A powerful gene-editing technique has been used to edit DNA directly in a person’s body — the first known instance of such a treatment.

The milestone treatment is part of a clinical trial of prime editing, a technique that can alter DNA with more precision than standard CRISPR–Cas9 methods can. In this case, prime editing was used to treat a condition called Wilson’s disease by rewriting DNA in liver cells, to erase a mutation that prevents them from eliminating excess copper.

Prime Medicine, a biotechnology company in Cambridge, Massachusetts, announced that it had treated the first person in its trial earlier this month. It expects to announce the first results from the study next year.

Bigger than CRISPR? A guide to the latest genome editors

Bigger than CRISPR? A guide to the latest genome editors

“I never dreamed that in my lifetime I would see this applied to my rare disease,” says Rhonda Rowland, president of the Wilson Disease Association in Atlanta, Georgia. “It’s going to be a really exciting year.”

In launching the trial, Prime Medicine joins a host of companies aiming to engineer cells directly in the body, rather than using the standard method of extracting a person’s cells, editing their DNA in a laboratory and then reinjecting the altered cells. Rewriting DNA in the body, or in vivo, is appealing because manufacturing and administering the treatment might be much cheaper and faster than making a bespoke therapy for each person from their own cells.

But in vivo approaches have their own challenges, says Krishanu Saha, a biomedical engineer at the University of Wisconsin–Madison. “It depends on what types of risks you’re willing to accept,” he says.

Wilson’s disease is caused by mutations in a gene called ATP7B, which encodes a protein that transports excess copper out of the liver. If left untreated, the resulting build-up of copper can cause liver and nerve damage, as well as neurological disorders.

People with Wilson’s disease are eager for a one-and-done treatment for their condition, says Rowland, rather than the current, complicated regimen of copper-clearing molecules and other medicines. And gene editing could, in theory, provide a lasting solution by correcting the faulty ATP7B gene.

So far, the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has approved only one gene-editing therapy, called Casgevy, which is used to treat two inherited blood disorders. Casgevy relies on CRISPR–Cas9 gene editing, which is often used to disable genes rather than to rewrite their sequences.

Bizarre CRISPR enzyme kills cancer cells by shredding their DNA

Bizarre CRISPR enzyme kills cancer cells by shredding their DNA

Another form of gene editing, called base editing, can rewrite individual DNA letters, but cannot make the particular corrections needed to fix the most common ATP7B mutations. That left prime editing, a more complex and versatile system that can insert, delete and rewrite segments of DNA. In another clinical trial, Prime Medicine used the technique to treat two people with a rare immune disorder, by rewriting DNA in each participant’s blood stem cells outside of the body and then injecting them back in.

So far, no gene-editing therapies have been approved for use in vivo. But the FDA is expected to issue a decision early next year about an in vivo CRISPR–Cas9 therapy for a condition called hereditary angioedema, which causes severe swelling.

#616. Giving Marjorie Taylor Greene a platform isn't good for America

Editor’s Note:  Dean Obeidallah, a former attorney, is the host of SiriusXM radio’s daily program “The Dean Obeidallah Show.” Follow him @DeanObeidallah@masto.ai. The opinions expressed in this commentary are his own. View more opinion on CNN.

Last year, GOP Rep. Marjorie Taylor Greene of Georgia spoke at a white nationalist event organized by Holocaust denier Nick Fuentes that caused Republican leaders to denounce her.

Last week, Greene’s Twitter account was temporarily suspended by the Elon Musk-headed platform over a tweet with a graphic referring to a “Trans Day of Vengeance,” as she denounced a planned transgender rights rally.

And come Tuesday, Greene has announced plans to protest in New York City when former President Donald Trump is expected to be arraigned on an indictment of more than 30 counts, calling the proceedings against him an “unconstitutional WITCH HUNT!”

But on Sunday, Greene was featured on CBS’ “60 Minutes” in an interview the long-running show promoted on Twitter with the tease: “Republican Rep. Marjorie Taylor Greene, nicknamed MTG, isn’t afraid to share her opinions, no matter how intense and in-your-face they are. She sits down with Lesley Stahl this Sunday on 60 Minutes.” The images attached to this tweet by “60 Minutes” include Greene and Stahl walking through the US Capitol, taking a stroll outside and Greene showing Stahl something on her phone.

It's time for Marjorie Taylor Greene to go

In the segment that aired Sunday night, Stahl noted the congresswoman had moved from the fringe to the GOP’s front row in two years despite a “sharp tongue” and “some pretty radical views” as well as “over the top” comments such as “the Democrats are a party of pedophiles.” Stahl also referred to video of Greene chasing a Parkland, Florida, school shooting survivor, still maintaining that the 2020 election was stolen and failing to criticize Trump over spending. (The interview was conducted before news of his indictment.)

But Stahl didn’t mention Greene spoke at a white nationalist event a year ago while a member of Congress or her extreme anti-Muslim views and her defense of January 6 rioters.

Criticism of CBS for amplifying Greene has been swift and well-deserved even before the program aired. Former GOP Rep. Adam Kinzinger of Illinois tweeted beforehand: “Wow. Insane that 60 min would do this.” (Kinzinger is a CNN senior political commentator.)

Journalist Molly Jong-Fast also slammed “60 Minutes” with the tweet: “Attention is currency and 60 minutes is spending its currency on the Jewish space lasers woman.” (Jong-Fast was apparently referring to Greene’s past claim that a massive California wildfire was started by “a laser” beamed from space controlled by a prominent Jewish banking family.)

David Hogg, who survived the 2018 horrific school shooting at Marjory Stoneman Douglas High School in Parkland and has since become an activist against gun violence, responded, “I look forward to your questions about why she thinks school shootings are fake and why she’s supported QAnon.”

Greene amplified the conspiracy theory — two years before being elected to Congress — that the Parkland shooting that took 17 lives was staged. And in 2019, Greene appeared on video confronting Hogg outside the Capitol when he was championing laws to save lives from gun violence, screaming that the then-teenager was a “coward.” She also called Hogg “#littleHitler” on social media.

Greene’s own tweet promoting Sunday’s segment was not filled with her typical smears of “fake news” when she doesn’t like the coverage. Rather, Greene urged people to tune in as she praised “60 Minutes” host Stahl (and misspelled her first name): “It was an honor to spend a few days with the legendary icon Leslie Stahl and talented crew @60Minutes.” Greene added, “Leslie is a trailblazer for women in journalism. And while we may disagree on some issues, I respect her greatly.”

Now, it is true that “60 Minutes” over its 50-plus-year history has featured what the show has dubbed “controversial” guests. These include a 2000 interview with Oklahoma City bomber Timothy McVeigh, whose 1995 terrorist attack left 168 dead, including 19 children. And the show did a 1979 interview with Iran’s Ayatollah Ruhollah Khomeini.

Perhaps “60 Minutes” views Greene — who has repeatedly downplayed and even defended the January 6, 2021, attack plus called for the GOP to become the party of “Christian nationalism” — in the vein of its long list of controversial guests. (CBS had not responded to a request from CNN for comment at time of publishing.)

However, the choice of Greene as a guest instantly recalls the comments of then-CBS CEO Les Moonves during Trump’s 2016 presidential campaign when he admitted that Trump’s candidacy “may not be good for America, but it’s damn good for CBS.” Moonves added, “The money’s rolling in and this is fun. … (T)his is going to be a very good year for us,” concluding, “Sorry. It’s a terrible thing to say. But bring it on, Donald. Keep going.”

Moonves may be gone from CBS, but it appears his mindset continues at “60 Minutes.” And that may be good for “60 Minutes,” but it’s definitely not good for America.
